definition.text: Land restoration, which may include rewilding, is returning land to a different or earlier state for a chosen purpose.

facts.text: Purposes include making land safe, stabilising ecological communities, cleaning up pollution, creating novel ecosystems or returning to a historical condition.
It is an antidote to damage caused mostly by people, such as pollution, deforestation, salination and species endangerment.
It differs from land reclamation, which alters or destroys ecosystems to make way for farming or building.
It can increase the supply of valuable ecosystem services.
Projects choose a reference ecosystem to measure success against and survey existing conditions first.
Traditional ecological knowledge used alongside Western science is becoming the mainstream approach.

title: Adaptive management

definition.text: Adaptive management is a way of managing natural resources while learning about them at the same time.

facts.text: It is the main method for running land restoration projects, because how nature responds to intervention is uncertain.
Changing a project's management as the ecosystem responds makes restoration better informed.
Forest landscape restoration combines adaptive management with other planning and appraisal methods.

definition.text: Restoring land lost to desertification, done in phases that first fix the soil and then enrich it.

facts.text: First, grasses, shelterbelts, windbreaks and woodlots fix the soil so dunes stop moving.
Shelterbelts are rows of trees set across the prevailing wind.
Next, nitrogen-fixing plants enrich the soil, crops are grown at once, and crops are rotated yearly to avoid draining trace elements.

definition.text: Mine reclamation is reshaping mined land so it again works as an ecosystem or can be used economically.

facts.text: It happens after mining ends, but may be planned before a mine is permitted.
The practice began at the start of the 20th century, and many abandoned mines were never reclaimed.
Full return to the original landscape is often impossible; usually the limit is making mine waste physically and chemically stable.
In open-cut mines, rock backfills the pit, stored soil and topsoil go on top, and vegetation is restored.
Reforestation is the main way of restoring post-mining sites.
Under the US 1977 SMCRA law, operators post a performance bond equal to the reclamation plan's cost, released only after reclamation succeeds.
A coal tax of $0.12 per ton underground and $0.28 per ton surface-mined funds reclamation of abandoned US mines.

definition.text: The Forestry Reclamation Approach (FRA) is a set of guidelines for regrowing forest on land mined for coal.

facts.text: It calls for at least four feet of good rooting material, such as topsoil or weathered sandstone, loosely graded to avoid compaction.
It plants early successional trees for wildlife and soil, then commercially valuable crop trees.

title: Novel ecosystem

definition.text: A novel ecosystem is one that human activity, land use and climate change have pushed into a mix of species and conditions never seen before.

facts.text: They are human-altered places where a self-sustaining ecosystem forms without ongoing human management.
The term was first used in 2006.
Defining features: change past a threshold, caused by people, and self-sustaining afterwards.
Without rapid climate action they could cover more than 50% of Earth's land by 2100 and 80% by 2300.
Examples include a quarry colonised by weedy species and coral reefs taken over by algae.
Some scientists argue that even if an ecosystem cannot return to its original state, a novel ecosystem's functions are still valuable.

contested_note: Researchers disagree on how to define novelty, and some argue against any sharp definition.

title: Managing novel ecosystems

definition.text: The choices for handling novel ecosystems: tolerating them, managing against them back toward history, or managing for them as new systems.

facts.text: Too little funding and information has made tolerance and inaction the default.
Managing against them means traditional restoration: removing non-native species and bringing back natives toward historical benchmarks.
Fast climate change often makes historical baselines unreachable, so scientists increasingly aim for resilient, adaptive ecosystems.

contested_note: Managing for novel ecosystems is described as more controversial than restoring historical states.

title: Anthromes
article: Novel ecosystem#Ecocentric approach to novel ecosystems

definition.text: Anthromes are the land's biomes in their modern, human-altered form, mapped by patterns of lasting human land use.

facts.text: Each anthrome is a patchwork of land uses, often with areas partly reclaimed by nature.
Groups include intensive land-use biomes such as croplands, pastures, plantations and cities, and artificial wetlands such as reservoirs and rice paddies.
